subject.title: fix(ci): bound linux-app-release git fetch with timeout

question: Should the Linux app release workflow treat any `origin/main` fetch exceeding 120 seconds as a hard pre-build failure without retry?
rationale: The implementation is technically sound, but the acceptable cutoff and retry policy determine release availability and require release-owner intent.

options.title: Accept the bounded cutoff
options.body: Merge the current implementation and treat a 120-second fetch as a failed release prerequisite that can be rerun.

options.title: Retry timeout exits
options.body: Add a small bounded retry loop for exit 124 or 137 before failing the release job, reducing transient aborts at the cost of a longer worst-case wait.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded cutoff
recommendation.body: Merge the current implementation and treat a 120-second fetch as a failed release prerequisite that can be rerun.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice changes Linux release orchestration, and this account has the strongest recent release-workflow ownership signal.
